taskPacket.objective: `node evals/run.mjs --class paired` runs declared arms over a corpus with a seeded shuffle, --repeat, a per-arm band, and delivery counted only as passing proofs with every guard passing (R2, R3).
instructions: Port the driver from origin/spike/orchestration-arms:spike/arms/ (measure.mjs, analyse.mjs, arm-faberun.mjs, arm-session.mjs, contract.mjs, corpus.mjs, fork.mjs, lib.mjs, prompt.mjs, checks/) into evals/paired/ as modules of this tree, and wire `--class paired` in evals/run.mjs through a module of its own. Arms are declared in evals/paired/arms.json with the spike's names (A, B, C, D, E, F-J) and runtimes; a corpus lives in evals/paired/corpus/<id>/.

Arms run in an order shuffled by a recorded seed, with --repeat <n>. The report gives per arm: proofs delivered, cost per delivered proof, wall clock, requests when the harness measures them, out-of-scope files, and the band: minimum and maximum always, and a 95% interval by resampling when n is 3 or more. It spends through evals/budget.mjs and refuses to start without --budget-usd.

R3: every hidden acceptance check has a kind, proof or guard. A run delivers the proofs that pass while every guard passes; an arm that changes nothing delivers zero. The acceptance runs on the arm's tree before any accepted file is restored over it (the spike's two measurement defects).

Write two proof tests in test/evals/paired.test.mjs, named exactly: the paired class reports a band per arm; and: a paired arm that changes nothing delivers zero. Both run the whole class with replay arms on a small fixture corpus; no provider.
decisions: This is campaign evals-with-a-budget of the leaving-home program; docs/campaigns/evals-with-a-budget/spec/SPEC.md is the source of truth for every requirement this node carries. Read the requirement text before writing code.

Follow AGENTS.md: plain ESM .mjs typed with JSDoc (npm run typecheck clean), no file over 800 lines (evals/run.mjs is already 710: new classes live in their own modules), no name exported from two modules, no duplicated top-level body, no barrel modules, no empty catch, a header comment on every new module saying what it owns and why it is separate, comments record measurement not intent.
Every new test file's first import is its scoped-home module (import "../scoped-home.mjs"); a source-shape ratchet enforces it.
No new runtime dependency. No test and no deterministic eval calls a provider: model-backed arms and judges run through the replay harness in tests. No test writes to the operator's real home.
The skill documents share one byte budget with 3 bytes of room: do not edit skills/faberun/SKILL.md or skills/faberun/references/*.md.
Do NOT edit .gitignore or any other ignore source. Never run git commit or git push: the controller seals and integrates your work.
The proof test is pinned: create it with exactly the name the Definition of Done quotes, in exactly the file it names; the DoD checks the name exists and runs it.

The spike code this campaign brings to main lives on the branch origin/spike/orchestration-arms, readable from this worktree with `git show origin/spike/orchestration-arms:<path>` and `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/spike/orchestration-arms -- spike/`. Bring it, do not rewrite it from zero, and keep the arm and hypothesis names of docs/campaigns/orchestration-arms/STATE.md.

Stochastic results belong in evals/results/<class>/ only when an operator runs a class for real. A test, a replay run and your own trial runs write their result to a temporary directory (make the result directory an option the tests pass); measured 2026-09-23, a first attempt of paired-class left evals/results/paired/<timestamp>.json in the tree and failed the node with unexpected_write.
Code, comments and documents are in English.
nonGoals: Running any stochastic eval with a real model (that is R11, the operator's step)

taskPacket.objective: `node evals/run.mjs --class judge-canary` scores a judge runtime by defect kind, and every paired and canary result names what produced it (R7, R8).
instructions: R7: `node evals/run.mjs --class judge-canary --runtime <id> --budget-usd <n> [--repeat <k>]` asks the judge through the product's own judge path, and reports per defect kind the recall (defects rejected with a finding citing the item), the false-alarm rate on clean cases and the cost per case, into evals/results/judge-canary/<date>-<runtime>.json. It spends through evals/budget.mjs.

R8: every paired and judge-canary result records the commit, the seed, the repetitions, the budget, priced spend, voided spend and, per runtime, harness, model and CLI version when the harness reports it. `--compare` accepts two results of the same class and refuses different classes.

Write two proof tests: in test/evals/judge-canary.test.mjs, named exactly: the canary scores a judge that always passes and one that always rejects (a replay judge that always passes has recall 0, one that always rejects has false alarm 1); and in test/evals/provenance.test.mjs, named exactly: a stochastic result names everything that produced it.
